text.p: Swedish metals and mining group Trelleborg AB said on Tuesday it was bidding 62.50 crowns per B-series share in Swedish rubber products and car components group Horda AB, valuing Horda at 276 million crowns.
Trelleborg said in a statement that it was offering 69 crowns for each Horda A-series share.
It said shareholders representing 89.7 percent of the votes in the company and 82.4 percent of the total Horda shares had indicated they would accept the offer.
Trelleborg said the acquisition would fit well into its strategy to strengthen its position within various business areas.

"The Trelleborg group has previously expressed its intention, through strategic acquisitions, of strengthening its rubber activities market position in several selected areas, such as components for the vehicle and building industries," it said.
"Acquiring Horda fits well into this strategy."
Trelleborg said that Horda's board had indicated the offer was favourable to shareholders and that the company needed more financial resources to expand.

The offer price was based on the average market price in the last three months, or a premium of 21 percent for the Horda's B share, Trelleborg said. Based on the average market price last month the premium was 17 percent, it said.
The subscription period for the offer runs from October 1 to October 25.
Horda's turnover in 1995 was 359 million crowns in vehicle components and rubber-related products.
Trelleborg Industri, Trelleborg's rubber operations, had a turnover of 5.1 billion crowns before the acquisition.
Trelleborg shares were one crown lower at 87.50 crowns at 1210 GMT. Horda shares rose four crowns to 62 crowns on news of the bid.
